critical_issues.msg: Date boundary is wrong: `beforeMs + 86400000` adds a full day, making '2026-05-13' include timestamps up to '2026-05-14 00:00:00' instead of '2026-05-13 23:59:59', leaking tasks from the next day.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the +86400000 or use `Date.toISOString().slice(0,10)` for consistent YYYY-MM-DD midnight-to-midnight comparison.

critical_issues.msg: list_tasks calls the DB twice: once for the actual page and again with page=1, page_size=10_000 just to count rows — loads up to 10,000 task rows into Python memory to get a total.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add a count method to TaskService (SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE tenant_id=...) and call it directly, or use SQL window function COUNT(*) OVER() in the same query to derive total without a second round-trip.

critical_issues.msg: tenant_id or 0 silently allows unauthenticated requests to operate as tenant 0 instead of being rejected — violates Rule 56 (authentication enforced correctly) and Rule 121 (router must not swallow auth failures).
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove or 0 fallback. If ctx.tenant_id is None after require_auth, the request should be rejected (401/403), not silently downgraded. Use: tenant_id: int = ctx.tenant_id (no fallback).

critical_issues.msg: user_id or 0 silently allows unauthenticated requests as user 0 instead of being rejected — same auth-bypass issue as tenant_id.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove or 0. Pass ctx.user_id directly; require_auth should guarantee it is set.

critical_issues.msg: load_dotenv() is called at module import time as a side effect — can silently override real environment variables in CI/production if .env is present with test-only values (Rule 128).
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the load_dotenv call entirely. If DATABASE_URL is needed in tests, it should come from a test-specific env mechanism or pytest fixture, not a module-level side effect.

critical_issues.msg: sys.path is mutated at module import time (Rule 128). This creates hidden global state that can break when project structure changes, and conflicts with any PYTHONPATH the runner already set.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the sys.path manipulation. The PYTHONPATH should be configured externally (e.g., in pytest.ini or the shell environment), not by mutating sys.path in conftest.py.

critical_issues.msg: Test file mocks TaskService at the module level (monkeypatch), bypassing the service layer entirely. This makes the file a router/HTTP-layer test, not a service-unit test, contradicting the project structure that requires mock_db_session fixtures with make_mock_session (Rule 61, Rule 67).
critical_issues.suggestion: Either (a) move this file to tests/integration/ and use real DB fixtures (per Rule 124), or (b) restructure it as a true unit test that calls service methods directly using make_mock_session with the session-scoped mock, so actual SQL patterns (multi-tenancy filtering, pagination, error cases) are exercised.

suggestions.msg: bulkComplete and bulkDelete run operations sequentially — N sequential API calls instead of parallel or batched.

suggestions.msg: filteredAndSorted is a pure function called twice per render (lines 144, 120) and also inside toggleSelectAll — expensive sort runs redundantly.
suggestions.suggestion: Memoize with useMemo: `const displayed = useMemo(() => filteredAndSorted(), [items, priorityFilter, assigneeFilter, createdAfter, createdBefore, sortKey, sortDir])`.

suggestions.msg: Assignee Select always renders with only the 'All Assignees' option — useUsers() is never called in this file, so the assignee filter dropdown is always empty.

suggestions.msg: Badge colorClass prop may not be the correct API — Badge component likely uses a `variant` prop instead.
suggestions.suggestion: Verify Badge component API; if it uses `variant`, change to `variant={STATUS_COLORS[...]} as const`.

suggestions.msg: isSubmitting passed as hardcoded false — the modal won't show a saving state for inline complete/delete in the list view.
suggestions.suggestion: Use update.isPending instead: `isSubmitting={update.isPending}`.

suggestions.msg: SortableContext receives non-standard `id` prop — only `items` and `strategy` are valid props in @dnd-kit/sortable

suggestions.msg: useTasks is called with hardcoded page=1 and empty search string, ignoring any user-provided filters
suggestions.suggestion: Expose filter/search state (page, search) via URL params or local state so the query reflects the UI

suggestions.msg: Drag-end status update swallows errors silently with empty catch block — user has no feedback on failure
suggestions.suggestion: Use React Query's onError callback or a toast/alert to surface the failure to the user

suggestions.msg: countByStatus is O(n) per column per render; recomputes on every state change for all 3 columns independently
suggestions.suggestion: Memoize with useMemo or pre-compute a status→count map once from allTasks

suggestions.msg: customerSearch state is set but never used — the Input has no onChange handler, so typing in the field has no effect
suggestions.suggestion: Add onChange to the Customer Input to update customerSearch, or remove customerSearch state and the useSearchCustomers hook entirely if search isn't needed

suggestions.msg: useSearchCustomers(customerSearch) always queries with the current search string; with no debounce, every keystroke fires a new request
suggestions.suggestion: Debounce the customerSearch state update (e.g., 300ms) before passing to useSearchCustomers

suggestions.msg: useOpportunities(1) and useUsers(1) have no page size or filter — likely loads all records into dropdowns, risking performance with large datasets
suggestions.suggestion: Add a reasonable page_size limit (e.g., 50–100) or server-side filtering for these dropdowns

suggestions.msg: customer_id field is a free-text Input accepting arbitrary strings — no validation or lookup UI to ensure it maps to a real customer
suggestions.suggestion: Replace free-text Input with a Select or Combobox using the customerData query results for validated selection

suggestions.msg: No loading or error states for usersData, customerData, or opportunitiesData — dropdowns render empty without any feedback while queries are pending or fail
suggestions.suggestion: Add isLoading checks or skeleton states for each query before rendering Select items

suggestions.msg: assigned_to defaults to string '0' as sentinel; the server expects number (line 81 converts it), but the default being string could cause subtle bugs if the conversion is skipped
suggestions.suggestion: Use null as sentinel instead of '0', or validate at the boundary before payload construction

suggestions.msg: unreadCount derives from notifData?.data?.total, not an actual unread flag — if total includes read notifications, the badge count is incorrect
suggestions.suggestion: Check the API response shape; if a separate unread_count or seen field exists, use that instead of total

suggestions.suggestion: Either connect useQuickAddTask to the TaskModal in page.tsx (adding isOpen and initialStatus from the store) or remove the quick-add button from the sidebar

suggestions.msg: Plus is imported but unused — the quick-add button uses it but the feature is disconnected (see line 132)
suggestions.suggestion: Remove unused import `Plus` if quick-add remains unconnected, or implement the feature end-to-end

suggestions.msg: useQuickAddTask is implemented but has no connected consumer — no component reads isOpen or initialStatus from this store, making it dead code
suggestions.suggestion: Either wire it to TaskModal in page.tsx (e.g., use useQuickAddTask to drive showCreate/createStatus) or remove the store entirely

suggestions.msg: SQLAlchemy warning filter is applied globally at module import time — a test-isolation violation (Rule 128). If a test accidentally generates a real warning, this suppression hides it in all tests.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the global filterwarnings call. If specific SQLAlchemy warnings must be suppressed, do it per-test inside the fixture that triggers them, using pytest.warns() or a local warnings.catch_warnings() context.

suggestions.msg: Lowercasing all SQL text (str(sql).lower()) before pattern matching means case-sensitive SQL written by the service will still match, but this also means any case-sensitive logic (e.g., quoted identifiers) would be silently broken — fragile design (Rule 19).
suggestions.suggestion: Document the lowercasing contract explicitly in the handler signature comment. All domain handlers must lowercase their sql_text checks consistently for this to work.

suggestions.msg: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] returns a bare MagicMock (no async context manager __aenter__/__aexit__) instead of a proper async session. If any test exercised the real session path, this would fail silently.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace lambda: MagicMock() with a proper async session mock or use make_mock_session() to keep consistency with the rest of the test infrastructure.

suggestions.msg: Tests only verify HTTP response codes, headers, and top-level serialization — they never assert on the actual SQL executed, multi-tenancy enforcement (tenant_id filtering), pagination correctness, or error-translation behavior. These are the most important invariants in the system (Rules 6, 7, 91).
suggestions.suggestion: Add service-level assertions: verify tenant_id is always included in SQL, page/page_size are passed through correctly, and service exceptions map to the expected HTTP codes.

issues.message: tenant_id or 0 silently allows unauthenticated requests to operate as tenant 0 instead of being rejected — violates Rule 56 (authentication enforced correctly) and Rule 121 (router must not swallow auth failures).

issues.message: load_dotenv() is called at module import time as a side effect — can silently override real environment variables in CI/production if .env is present with test-only values (Rule 128).
issues.suggestion: Remove the load_dotenv call entirely. If DATABASE_URL is needed in tests, it should come from a test-specific env mechanism or pytest fixture, not a module-level side effect.

issues.message: sys.path is mutated at module import time (Rule 128). This creates hidden global state that can break when project structure changes, and conflicts with any PYTHONPATH the runner already set.
issues.suggestion: Remove the sys.path manipulation. The PYTHONPATH should be configured externally (e.g., in pytest.ini or the shell environment), not by mutating sys.path in conftest.py.

issues.message: SQLAlchemy warning filter is applied globally at module import time — a test-isolation violation (Rule 128). If a test accidentally generates a real warning, this suppression hides it in all tests.
issues.suggestion: Remove the global filterwarnings call. If specific SQLAlchemy warnings must be suppressed, do it per-test inside the fixture that triggers them, using pytest.warns() or a local warnings.catch_warnings() context.

issues.message: Lowercasing all SQL text (str(sql).lower()) before pattern matching means case-sensitive SQL written by the service will still match, but this also means any case-sensitive logic (e.g., quoted identifiers) would be silently broken — fragile design (Rule 19).
issues.suggestion: Document the lowercasing contract explicitly in the handler signature comment. All domain handlers must lowercase their sql_text checks consistently for this to work.

parsed.summary: conftest.py works correctly but has three module-level import-time side effects (load_dotenv, sys.path mutation, global warning filter) that violate test isolation and the project's own rules.

issues.message: Test file mocks TaskService at the module level (monkeypatch), bypassing the service layer entirely. This makes the file a router/HTTP-layer test, not a service-unit test, contradicting the project structure that requires mock_db_session fixtures with make_mock_session (Rule 61, Rule 67).
issues.suggestion: Either (a) move this file to tests/integration/ and use real DB fixtures (per Rule 124), or (b) restructure it as a true unit test that calls service methods directly using make_mock_session with the session-scoped mock, so actual SQL patterns (multi-tenancy filtering, pagination, error cases) are exercised.

issues.message: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] returns a bare MagicMock (no async context manager __aenter__/__aexit__) instead of a proper async session. If any test exercised the real session path, this would fail silently.
issues.suggestion: Replace lambda: MagicMock() with a proper async session mock or use make_mock_session() to keep consistency with the rest of the test infrastructure.

issues.message: Tests only verify HTTP response codes, headers, and top-level serialization — they never assert on the actual SQL executed, multi-tenancy enforcement (tenant_id filtering), pagination correctness, or error-translation behavior. These are the most important invariants in the system (Rules 6, 7, 91).
issues.suggestion: Add service-level assertions: verify tenant_id is always included in SQL, page/page_size are passed through correctly, and service exceptions map to the expected HTTP codes.

parsed.summary: test_tasks.py tests HTTP endpoint behavior well but mocks out the entire service layer, leaving the most important logic (SQL generation, multi-tenancy, service errors) untested at the unit level.
